title: Viva Piñata: Trouble in Paradise
subtitle: Make a garden worth visiting

body: Viva Piñata: Trouble in Paradise is Rare's Xbox 360 gardening simulation, released in North America on 2 September 2008. The player reshapes a patch of land to attract brightly coloured piñata creatures, learning what each species needs before it will settle there. Plants, ponds and other residents turn the garden into a network of requirements. The sequel expands the original's collection and adds cooperative play, allowing another gardener to help with the same space. Its gentle appearance hides a game about observation, planning and managing the consequences of each new arrival.

A creature may need a particular plant, terrain or food source before becoming a resident. Meeting that condition can attract something else, so one improvement often begins another chain of decisions. The Piñarctic and Dessert Desert provide separate areas where creatures can be trapped and brought home. Sand and ice can later be introduced to the main garden to support them. An encyclopedia records preferences, giving the player a practical way to turn curiosity into a plan. The garden grows through these relationships rather than through decoration alone.

Two players can garden locally, with larger cooperative groups originally supported through Xbox Live. A Just for Fun mode removes several restrictions and threats, offering an easier space for experimentation. The Xbox Live Vision camera can read special cards to introduce creatures or items, connecting a physical collectible to the garden. Grant Kirkhope composed the music. Trouble in Paradise later joined Rare Replay on Xbox One, carrying its expanded version of the original idea to another console. Its pleasures remain the small discoveries that follow a carefully made change.
